name: Act of July 15, 1870 providing for the collection of Kickapoo roving on the Texas and Mexico borders and their location in Indian Territory
aka: Indian appropriation act of July 15, 1870, Kickapoo clause
landTaken: The Commission found the Oklahoma reservation contained 206,466 acres, of which about 184,300 were ceded in 1891 and the rest mostly allotted to tribal members (Docket 318).
compensation: The Commission found the 1891 agreement paid $64,650.00 in cash, and that in 1908 Congress, on the Kickapoo's petition, appropriated $215,000 more, a total of $279,650. The Docket 318 compromise added $273,250; the tribe's general council approved it 38 to 7 on August 3, 1968.
today: This Act took no land. The reservation later set apart (Royce Area 650) was ceded by the agreement of September 9, 1891, ratified March 3, 1893, recorded in cession-1893-03-03-kickapoo; the Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma's claim that its price was unconscionable was settled by compromise for $273,250 in 1969 (Docket 318). The Commission found the Kickapoo received title to the reservation as of October 1, 1874 as a gratuity from the United States.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says the Kickapoo forcibly removed from Texas in 1839 went to Mexico, where they held a land grant for guarding its northern border, that many from Indian Territory rejoined them during the Civil War, and that in 1873 a military scheme forced some of the Mexican Kickapoo to move to Indian Territory.

promises: No treaty. Congress appropriated up to $25,000 to enable the Secretary of the Interior to collect bands of Kickapoo or other Indians roving on the borders of Texas and Mexico and to locate and subsist them in the Indian Territory.
The reservation where they were settled (Royce Area 650) was set apart later by the President, according to Royce, in 1883.

openQuestions: treaties.json: this entry and cession-1871-03-03-kickapoo are two appropriation acts, not cessions, and both point to Royce 650, the reservation later set apart for the Mexican Kickapoo and ceded in 1891.
The settlement is counted as litigation only. Whether the 1891 agreement was obtained improperly, which the 1908 appropriation may reflect, was not found in a government or court source opened.
No Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma or Kickapoo Traditional Tribe of Texas account was opened; the Oklahoma tribe's website was not found by search.

Audit 2026-11-08: downgraded contested -> no-breach-found. This appropriation act took no land and made no promise to the Kickapoo that was later broken; the Docket 318 compromise concerns the 1891 cession, which has its own file (cession-1893-03-03-kickapoo). The litigation breach was removed here and pointed to in today, matching the treatment of the 1872 Ute negotiation act.

plain.promised: No treaty. In 1870 Congress paid to gather Kickapoo living on the Texas and Mexico borders and settle them in Indian Territory, where a reservation was later set apart.
plain.happened: This Act took no land. The reservation later set apart was ceded in 1891; that cession, and the claim over its price, is recorded separately.
plain.today: The Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma's claim over the 1891 price was settled by compromise for $273,250 in 1969.
